status: optional planner follow-up; default vendor unchanged

protocol.scope: Remove ANSI predicate widening only when integer operands can be represented exactly at FLOAT precision relative to Spark DOUBLE coercion. Small signed widths are exact for every value. Other numeric literals require a successful direct numeric literal evaluation; unknown or lossy values retain DOUBLE.
protocol.capture_format_correction: Wrap BOOLEAN predicates in INT casts for the existing numeric comparator; the original failed comparison and captures are preserved in failed-capture-00.
limits: No runtime inspection of INT/BIGINT column values
No string literal folding or arbitrary constant evaluation
Preserve dynamic INT/BIGINT widening and the separate unsigned/decimal/DOUBLE paths

implementation.rule: Keep FLOAT for TINYINT/SMALLINT and INT/BIGINT literals whose Spark DOUBLE value survives a FLOAT round trip exactly. Keep DOUBLE for dynamic INT/BIGINT, inexact literals and unrecognized expressions.
implementation.reuse: Extract and reuse the existing direct numeric literal evaluator; no execution kernel or new dependency.
implementation.proof_boundary: All predicate results are BOOLEAN. Every FLOAT value embeds exactly into DOUBLE, so order/equality against an integer also representable at FLOAT precision is unchanged, including the existing NaN/zero normalization. BIGINT proof uses its rounded DOUBLE value.

correctness.error_text_note: Four existing failed casts report a different invalid input value; no status, rows, types or other actual fields change.

performance_protocol.purpose: Measure the safe narrowing optimization against the corrected parent and compare selected equal-result inputs with the original pre-fix runtime. Dynamic INT/BIGINT precision protection must remain.
performance_protocol.inference: Process medians are the unit; report paired quartet log ratios with fixed seed 172 and 10000-resample percentile intervals. Retain all observations including failed controls. No uniform no-regression claim or threshold-based retries.
performance_protocol.runtime: parent d6540c1 plus only the safe-narrowing planner patch; no type-inference shortcut or hash diagnostics

pre_fix_comparison.note: The pre-fix runtime is not Spark-compatible at integer precision boundaries. These benchmark inputs have equal outputs; correctness uses the corrected parent as baseline.

performance_findings: Relative to the corrected parent, SMALLINT column comparison, exact integer literal comparison and constant IN execute about 13-14 percent faster, with 10-14 percent fewer instructions.

Direct pre-fix comparisons for those three cases have conditional intervals spanning zero and execution instruction differences within 0.01 percent. This removes their added widening work on the tested inputs.
Dynamic INT column comparison still uses DOUBLE and is about 15 percent slower than pre-fix, with about 11.7 percent more instructions. That local cost remains.

The unchanged explicit-DOUBLE control rises about 1.2 percent against the parent, while a same-parent INT control shifts about 5.8 percent without changed instruction work. Retain these observations; no blanket no-regression claim is made.
source_difference: The parent and narrowed benchmark builds differ only in common.rs; benchmark, dependency and other runtime sources are identical.
baseline_reuse: The parent probe and benchmark binaries are reused from d6540c1 with recorded hashes. Existing 6068 before captures are reused from that identical parent probe; new/ANSI/zero and all candidate captures are fresh.
setup_correction: The initial 31 predicates produced BOOLEAN output, unsupported by the existing numeric comparator. Wrap only their outputs in CAST(... AS INT), preserving NULL, and recapture Spark and Rust. Predicate set and candidate logic are unchanged; initial captures and failed comparison are retained.
limitations: Only the documented predicate precision rule is optimized. Other constant expressions and dynamic INT/BIGINT retain the widening cost.
The existing signed-zero GROUP BY and JOIN USING differences remain outside this change.
The coarse corpus excludes schema metadata and structured error equality and is not complete Spark compatibility.
Measurements are bounded to this machine, preloaded inputs and the fixed schedule; controls show timing variation.
The separate type-inference shortcut stays deferred and unapplied. No original timing interval is declared resolved.
